name: K'ap Tái Shap
description: K'ap Tái Shap (Big Collecting Tens) is an expanded version of K'ap Shap, designed for larger groups (up to 20 players) and utilizing multiple sets of Chinese dominoes (up to 8 sets). It is a high-stakes, fast-paced game where the goal is to form a specific combination of identical pairs and 10/20-sum pairs. The use of multiple sets introduces high duplication, changing the strategy from simple matching to probability-based hoarding.

history.origins: Developed as a social club variant of K'ap Shap in Hong Kong and Guangdong, where large groups needed a game that could accommodate everyone at a single table.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Popularized in Cantonese gambling halls ('Fan-Tan' houses).
1950s: Becomes a staple in Southeast Asian Chinese communities.
Present: Still played in traditional social clubs ('Tongs') and elders' associations.
history.cultural: Reflects the collectivist and high-entropy nature of Chinese social gaming.
history.evolution: The 'Tái' (Big) refers both to the number of players and the 'Big' sets of dominoes used.

setup.deck: Usually one set per every 2-3 players. For 10 players, 4 sets (128 tiles) is standard.
setup.dealing: Standard 10/9 tile split. Tiles are shuffled face-down and built into a long wall (the 'Dragon').
setup.equipment: Multiple sets of Chinese dominoes, flat playing surface, chips or counters for stakes

rules.objective: Complete a winning hand of five pairs (one identical 'Eye' and four 10/20-sum pairs).
rules.gameplay:
1. Drawing and discarding proceed counter-clockwise.
2. In K'ap Tái Shap, any player can shout 'K'ap!' to take a discard out of turn IF it completes their winning hand (similar to Mahjong).
keyRules: A winning hand requires exactly one identical pair (ngán/eye) from either Civil or Military series
Four additional pairs must each total exactly 10 or 20 pips
The 4-2 tile counts as 3 pips (not 6) when calculating pair totals
Players may call 'K'ap!' to claim a discard out of turn if it completes their hand
First player starts with 10 tiles; others start with 9 tiles
Discards are placed face-up and available for any player to claim

strategy.basic: With multiple sets, it is much easier to find an identical 'Eye'. Focus on the 'Sum-Pairs' first, as they determine the flow of your hand.
strategy.intermediate: Hoarding: If you see that 6-6 tiles are appearing frequently in discards, start hoarding 4-4 or 3-1 to complete 10/20 sums. The Big game is about recognizing high-volume numbers.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: Observe the 'Sum' your neighbors are building. If your neighbor is picking up low-value tiles (1s and 2s), don't discard any 8s or 9s—you are likely giving them their 10-sum.
tips: The 4-2 tile is extremely powerful in the Big variant because it can bridge both 10 and 20 target sums depending on whether you count it as 6 or 3.
Don't wait for a 'Three Nobles' combination unless you have 3/4 of the pieces; it's too slow for this fast variant.

scoring.description: The game is typically played for a pot funded by equal antes from all players. The winner collects the entire pot.
scoring.winCondition: First player to form a complete winning hand with one identical pair and four scoring pairs (10 or 20 pips each).

synthesis.shortDescription: A multi-player Chinese domino game for up to 20 players using multiple domino sets. Race to form one identical pair and four pairs totaling 10 or 20 pips.
